text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key habit is following naming conventions: use clear names for variables and functions so readers know what they mean. Another good practice is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because fixing bugs or adding new features takes less time. Remember, code is read far more often than it is written, so always write with your readers in mind.
